Qatar is one of the world's largest exporters of liquefied natural gas

Siddarth S, Jana Choukeir and Nayera Abdallah | Reuters News

Qatar's budget deficit ballooned to 21.2 billion riyals ($5.82 billion) in the second quarter of 2026, government data showed on Tuesday, compared to 757 million riyals in the same period a year ago, due primarily to the Iran war's hit to oil and gas revenues.

Qatar is one of the world's largest exporters of liquefied natural gas (LNG), which is a major contributor to government income. It has faced production shortages due to damage caused by the conflict.

On an annual basis, total revenues for the second quarter sank 57.1% to 25.64 billion riyals, data from the finance ministry showed.

Oil and gas revenues plunged to 874 million riyals in the second quarter from 34 billion in the same period a year earlier.

Non-oil and gas revenues for the second quarter dipped about 4.2% to 24.77 billion riyals on an annual basis.

Total public spending in the second quarter fell to 46.87 billion riyals compared to 60.60 billion riyals a year earlier.

Qatar had posted a deficit of $2.83 billion in the first quarter of this year.

(Reporting by Siddarth S, Jana Choukeir and Nayera Abdallah; Editing by Alison Williams and Joe Bavier)
